1.why: All nine screens use a clean, static layout with no moving images or pop-ups visible.

2.why: Page headings, field labels, status messages, and primary teal action buttons are visually prominent.

3.why: Each screen focuses on one main task and presents the relevant field and action near the center.

4.why: The user must complete nine screens and retain password rules, a recovery code, a new password, and an MFA code.

5.why: No password-manager prompt, autofill control, remember-me option, or equivalent memory aid is visible.

6.why: Previously entered values such as the recovery identifier and code remain visible on some screens, but no saved-account or familiar-item interface is shown.

7.why: Most instructions are brief, plainly worded, and displayed in readable text with clear headings.

8.why: No error state or corrective error message is shown in any of the screenshots.

9.why: The interface states requirements such as six digits and 12 password characters but provides no concrete input examples.

10.why: The system requires a password and codes in sequence but does not present clear alternative authentication choices such as face login.

11.why: Each screen presents only one or two primary choices at a time.

12.why: Visible status text and logs report outcomes such as recovery preparation, password acceptance, privacy acceptance, and appointment confirmation.

13.why: Each new step includes a short instruction, and several screens include highlighted security reminders.

14.why: Controls such as Start over and Forgot password support recovery, but no failed-attempt screen demonstrates an easy retry process.

15.why: The same header, card layout, typography, colors, button styles, reminder panels, and logs are used consistently across all screens.
